transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Honestly, I’m mostly here because other people sort of pushed me to come. HR at work has made a few comments, and my sister’s been on me about it too—saying I’ve gotten too thin, that it’s noticeable, that I don’t look like myself. I don’t know, from my side it doesn’t feel as dramatic as they make it sound. I just see that my suits fit sharper now, more cleanly, and I guess my weight has kept dropping since the divorce. But they’re worried enough that I figured I should come in and talk to someone.
Have you been deliberately eating less or avoiding certain foods to lose weight or keep from gaining weight?

Yeah… I mean, I guess if I’m being honest, yes, I do keep it pretty limited. I don’t always think of it as “deliberately” in this dramatic way, but most days I’ll just have coffee in the morning, and then if I’m out between sales calls I might have a protein bar, something quick that doesn’t feel like a whole meal. Then at night I’ll do something small, like grilled chicken, but I’ll skip the rice or anything like that.

It’s not like I sit there with some big plan written out, but I do avoid things that feel like they’ll make me gain or like they’ll undo the day. Once I start eating a full meal, it feels like I’ve messed up the whole day, and then I get really frustrated with myself. So it’s easier to just keep it controlled and simple.

Have you ever made yourself sick or used medications like laxatives or diet pills to control your weight after eating? Or do you ever feel like you have to exercise a lot to 'burn off' the food you've eaten?

I don’t really know how to answer that neatly. I mean, I don’t think of myself as someone who does that kind of thing. I’m not, like… planning out some whole routine after meals or anything.

As far as making myself sick, no, I haven’t done that. And I’m not taking anything like that to deal with food, at least not in the way you’re asking. The exercise thing is harder, because I do feel better when I’ve moved around, but I wouldn’t say I’m going to the gym for hours to punish myself after eating. It’s more that if I’ve had more than I expected, I get kind of restless and uncomfortable, and I’ll want to be active or walk it off, I guess. But I’m not sure if that counts as “having to” exercise a lot. It doesn’t feel that extreme to me.
Do you find yourself being very afraid of gaining weight or becoming fat, even if others might see you as underweight?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t love the word “afraid,” because it makes it sound kind of irrational or dramatic, but yes, I guess that’s what it is.

Like, if I have a client dinner and I eat more than I normally would, or if I’m away for a weekend in Miami and there’s drinks and restaurant food and everything is less controlled, I’ll come back and check the scale, and if it’s even a pound higher, I feel this immediate panic. It’s not just, “Oh, that’s annoying.” It feels like I’m losing control, like if I don’t get on top of it right away it’s going to keep going.

And then I start doing the math in my head, like, okay, tomorrow I’ll cut back, I’ll keep it lighter, I’ll be more careful. I know other people might look at me and say I don’t need to worry about that, but when I see the number go up, even a little, it really gets under my skin.
Do you see yourself as overweight or in need of further weight loss, even when others might tell you that you're already underweight or too thin?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d say I look at myself and think, like, “I’m huge” or something that obvious. But I definitely don’t see what other people seem to be seeing.

It’s more specific than that. Like, if I’m getting ready for a meeting, or a date, or even just trying on a shirt before going out, I’ll end up staring at my stomach and my face. I’ll turn sideways in the mirror, check my jaw, check if my shirt is pulling anywhere, and if I think I look soft at all, it just… it really bothers me. It’s hard to shake. I start thinking people are going to notice and see me as sloppy, or weak, or like I don’t have discipline.

And people have told me I’m thin, or that I don’t need to lose anything, but it doesn’t land that way when I’m looking at myself. I can hear them say it, and part of me understands they probably mean it, but then I look in the mirror and I’m focused on the one area that looks wrong to me. So yes, I guess I do feel like there’s still something I need to fix.
